title: What Rivermark Is Worth
description: Somewhere in eleven presses of paper there is a number with the town's name against it. It will be a small number.

the_figure.title: The figure
the_figure.objective: Every drawer in the long room is labelled by year and by hundred. Find the one Rivermark is in.
the_figure.journal: The long room is not locked and the drawers are labelled in one hand and there is no reason on earth why I should not open them. That is the third time this week that a thing has been left open to me and I have found it worse than a lock.

found_the_number.title: Sheet six
found_the_number.journal: Rivermark: eleven hundred souls, four hundred and six roofs, a granary, a bridge, two mills of which one is burnt, and a total. The total is less than the crane on the new landing cost. It is not written cruelly. It is not written at all — it is added up, in a column, between a weir and a stand of oak, by somebody being paid by the day to add things up.

did_not_look.title: Left in the drawer
did_not_look.journal: I stood in front of the drawer with my hand on it for a while. There is a version of this where I never know the number and the number does not exist, and I am aware that it is not a very good version, and I closed the press anyway.
